### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 1) — 2 marks

> Where do we keep our money safe? If we want immediate cash where do we go and withdraw money?

- **Answer: We keep our money safe in a bank. For immediate cash we go to an ATM (or the bank) and withdraw money.**
- Answer points:
  - Money is kept safe in a bank (1 mark)
  - Immediate cash: go to an ATM (the bank counter is also accepted) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Bank for keeping money safe AND ATM (or bank) for immediate cash.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part correct.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part correct.
- Model answer: We keep our money safe in a bank. For immediate cash we go to an ATM and withdraw money.
- Marking guide: Part 1: bank / the bank / in the bank (also "bank account", "savings account"). Part 2: ATM / ATM machine / Automated Teller Machine; "bank" is also accepted, since money can be withdrawn at the bank counter. Accept the Hindi "bank" spelt any way.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.8 l.4-15
- Teacher note: The header prints "Total No. of printed pages: 09", but the paper has 8 pages ("Page 1 of 8" … "Page 8 of 8") and nothing is missing: Q1–Q15 run without a gap and the marks add up to 80. For part 2, both "ATM" and "bank" are defensible, so both get the mark.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 2) — 2 marks

> Identify this bird and write its name. How does this bird move in water?

- **Answer: It is a duck. It swims (paddles) in water with its webbed feet.**
- Answer points:
  - Name: duck (mallard) (1 mark)
  - Moves in water by swimming / paddling with its webbed feet (floating also accepted) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Names the duck AND says it swims / paddles with webbed feet.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part correct (e.g. "duck" but no movement, or "it swims" with a wrong name).
  - none (0 marks): Neither part correct.
- Model answer: This is a duck. It swims in water by paddling with its webbed feet.
- Marking guide: Name: duck, ducks, mallard, mallard duck, wild duck, drake, batakh / bathak / badak (Hindi), bathu (Telugu), vaathu (Tamil), baatu (Kannada), tharavu (Malayalam). Not "swan", "goose" or "hen". Movement: swims, paddles, floats and swims, "uses its webbed feet like oars", "with the help of webbed feet". "Floats" alone gets the mark too.
- Source: Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook); webbed feet: Ch 3 (deev103), p.16 l.17-19
- Teacher note: Ducks are not named in the Chapter 1–5 text; the textbook explains webbed feet for swimming with turtles (Ch 3). This is general knowledge, so the parent checks the wording.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 3) — 2 marks

> What kind of food group is this? Name any two food items from this group.

- **Answer: Body-building foods (protein-rich foods). Any two of: egg, chicken/meat, fish, milk, paneer/cheese, beans/rajma/pulses (dal), peanuts.**
- Answer points:
  - Food group: body-building foods / protein-rich foods (1 mark)
  - First correct food item from this group (0.5 marks)
  - Second correct food item from this group (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Correct food group (body-building / protein) AND two correct food items.
  - partial-high (1.5 marks): Food group correct and only one correct food item.
  - partial-low (0.5 marks): Only one correct food item and nothing else.
  - partial (1 mark): Food group correct but no correct items, or two correct items but the group missing or wrong.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: These are body-building foods (protein foods). Examples: eggs and fish.
- Marking guide: Group: body-building food(s), body building food, protein food(s), protein-rich food, proteins, "food that helps us grow". Items: egg(s), chicken, meat, mutton, fish, milk, cheese, paneer, beans, rajma, kidney beans, pulses, dal, lentils, chana / chickpeas, soybean, tofu, peanuts, groundnuts, almonds, walnuts, curd. "Energy-giving" or "protective" for the group gets 0 for that part.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.7-18
- Teacher note: The textbook calls this group "body-building foods"; "protein" is the word on the printed picture (a shaker labelled PROTEIN, not redrawn here). Accept either name.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 4) — 2 marks

> Name the person who fixes the wires . Write the name of any tool which he uses.

- **Answer: Electrician. Tools: screwdriver, pliers, tester, wire cutter, wire stripper or insulation tape (any one).**
- Answer points:
  - The person is an electrician (1 mark)
  - Any one tool, e.g. screwdriver, pliers, tester, wire cutter, insulation tape (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Electrician AND one correct tool.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part correct.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part correct.
- Model answer: He is an electrician. He uses a screwdriver.
- Marking guide: Person: electrician, electrition (spelling), lineman, wireman, "bijli wala", "light man", "current man". Tool: screwdriver, pliers / plier / plas, tester / line tester / screwdriver tester, wire cutter, wire stripper, insulation tape / black tape, multimeter, drill, spanner, hammer, ladder, torch. Safety gear he is shown wearing (helmet, rubber gloves) is also accepted, since the question asks what he uses.
- Source: Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook)
- Teacher note: Printed with a space before the full stop ("wires ."), kept. Electricians and their tools are not in the Chapter 1–5 text; this is general knowledge.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 5) — 2 marks

> Identify the device and write its name. Write any one benefit of using this device.

- **Answer: Solar cooker. Benefit: it cooks food using sunlight, so it saves gas, fuel and electricity and does not pollute the air (no smoke or ash).**
- Answer points:
  - Name: solar cooker (1 mark)
  - One benefit: uses free sunlight / saves gas, fuel or electricity / no smoke or ash, does not pollute (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Solar cooker AND one correct benefit.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part correct.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part correct.
- Model answer: It is a solar cooker. It cooks food with sunlight and does not make smoke, so it does not pollute the environment.
- Marking guide: Name: solar cooker, solar oven, sun cooker, box solar cooker. Benefit: cooks with sunlight; saves gas / LPG / fuel / wood / electricity / money; no smoke or ash; does not pollute; environment-friendly; sunlight is free and never runs out.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.14 l.19-25

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q4 · Q4 — 3 marks

> Match the method of cooking and with its name.

- Pairs:
  - Picture 1 → boiling
  - Picture 2 → steaming
  - Picture 3 → grilling
  - Picture 4 → frying
  - Picture 5 → roasting
  - Picture 6 → baking
- **Answer: 1 – boiling; 2 – steaming; 3 – grilling (or roasting); 4 – frying; 5 – roasting (or grilling); 6 – baking.**
- Answer points:
  - Picture 1 (eggs in bubbling water) – boiling (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 2 (food on trays above water, covered) – steaming (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 3 (food on a rack under a hot element) – grilling or roasting (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 4 (patties in oil in a pan) – frying (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 5 (food on a grate over hot coals) – roasting or grilling (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 6 (muffins in an oven) – baking (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All six pictures matched correctly (pictures 3 and 5 may take grilling and roasting either way round).
  - partial (1.5 marks): Three pictures matched correctly (½ each); give ½ for every correct pair.
  - none (0 marks): No correct pair.
- Marking guide: ½ mark per correct pair. Pictures 3 (oven rack under a hot element) and 5 (barbecue grate over coals) can each be called grilling or roasting: accept 3 – grilling, 5 – roasting, or 3 – roasting, 5 – grilling.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.13 l.18-26
- Teacher note: Printed marks are "3 x 1 = 3M", but there are six pictures and six names, so each pair is marked ½ (6 × ½ = 3). The printed instruction has a stray "and" ("cooking and with its name"), kept. Pictures 3 and 5 both show food cooked by direct dry heat on a rack/grate, so grilling and roasting are accepted for either.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q5 · e) — 1 mark

> Encircle the national emblem of our country on the above note.

- **Answer: The Lion Capital of Ashoka (three lions on a base with a wheel, "Satyamev Jayate" below) on the right side of the front of the note is circled.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): The national emblem (lions on the base with the wheel) on the front of the note is circled.
  - partial (0.5 marks): The circle is near the emblem but also takes in other large parts of the note.

- Teacher note: The national emblem (Lion Capital of Ashoka) is not in the Chapter 1–5 text; this is general knowledge. Do this on the printed sheet.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q6 · b) — 1 mark

- Also accept: bajra · bajara · bajri · bajre · pearl millet · millet · millets · bajra millet · sajje · sajjalu · kambu · kambam · cumbu · bajra roti

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q8 · 1. — 1 mark

> Ant Wasp Butterfly Termite

- Options: Ant · Wasp · Butterfly · Termite
- **Answer: Butterfly · Termite**
- Marking guide: Butterfly: ants, wasps and termites live together in colonies (nests) and can bite or sting; a butterfly does not. Termite: ants, wasps and butterflies all visit flowers or feed on sweet things like nectar, while termites eat wood (and termites are the only one not named in the textbook). Either gets the mark.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q8 · 3. — 1 mark

> Marigold Tulsi Amla Ajwain

- Options: Marigold · Tulsi · Amla · Ajwain
- **Answer: Marigold · Amla**
- Marking guide: Marigold: a flower used for colour (natural dye), while tulsi, amla and ajwain are used as medicine / food. Amla: a fruit, while tulsi and ajwain are kept in the textbook's home-remedy table and marigold is a flower. Either gets the mark.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 1. — 3 marks

> What is Van Mahotsav? When is it celebrated?

- **Answer: Van Mahotsav is the Tree Planting Festival of India. People plant trees to protect the environment and make the earth greener. It is celebrated every year in the rainy season, from 1 July to 7 July.**
- Answer points:
  - It is the tree planting festival (people plant trees) (1 mark)
  - Why: to protect the environment / make the earth greener (1 mark)
  - When: every year in the rainy season, 1 to 7 July (first week of July) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Says it is the tree planting festival, why trees are planted, and that it is celebrated from 1 to 7 July (rainy season).
  - partial-high (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - partial (1 mark): One of the three points.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Van Mahotsav is the Tree Planting Festival. People plant trees to protect the environment and make the earth greener. It is celebrated every year in the rainy season, from 1st to 7th July.
- Marking guide: For "when", accept "1–7 July", "first week of July", "in July" or "in the rainy season".
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.6 l.2-12

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 2. — 3 marks

> Who is a nature scientist? Write about its role.

- **Answer: A nature scientist is a person who studies plants and animals. Role: observes and studies plants, animals and birds in forests; guides people (like students on a nature trail) in exploring nature; tells us not to harm plants and animals and helps protect them.**
- Answer points:
  - A person who studies plants and animals (nature) (1 mark)
  - Role: observes / studies / identifies plants, animals and birds in their habitat (1 mark)
  - Role: guides others in exploring nature and teaches them to protect it (do not harm plants and animals) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Correct meaning plus two roles.
  - partial-high (2 marks): Correct meaning plus one role, or two roles without the meaning.
  - partial (1 mark): Only the meaning, or only one role.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: A nature scientist is a person who studies plants and animals. Abha Didi, a nature scientist, guided the students through the forest at Pachmarhi, told them about the birds and animals there, and taught them not to harm plants and animals.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.4 l.5-14
- Teacher note: Printed "its role" (for a person) kept. The textbook defines a nature scientist; the roles are drawn from what Abha Didi does in Ch 3, so the parent judges the wording.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 3. — 3 marks

> What is a balanced diet?

- **Answer: A balanced diet (balanced plate) has food in the right quantities from all three food groups — protective foods (fruits and vegetables) the most, then body-building foods and some energy-giving foods — along with water. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.**
- Answer points:
  - Food from all three food groups (energy-giving, body-building, protective) (1 mark)
  - In the right quantities (more fruits and vegetables, some body-building and energy foods), with water (1 mark)
  - It keeps us healthy, active and strong / helps the body grow (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All three food groups, right quantities, and why it is needed.
  - partial-high (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - partial (1 mark): One point.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: A balanced diet has all three food groups — energy-giving, body-building and protective foods — in the right amounts, with plenty of fruits and vegetables and enough water. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.
- Marking guide: Naming the three groups with an example each also earns the first point.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.8 l.25-30; Ch 5 (deev105), p.8 l.1-5

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 4. — 3 marks

> Write the full form of ATM. Write any two uses of ATM.

- **Answer: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine. Uses: to take out (withdraw) money at any time; to check the bank balance; to deposit money; to get a mini statement; to change the PIN.**
- Answer points:
  - Full form: Automated Teller Machine (1 mark)
  - First use, e.g. take out money any time (1 mark)
  - Second use, e.g. check balance / deposit money / mini statement / change PIN / transfer money (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Correct full form and two correct uses.
  - partial-high (2 marks): Full form and one use, or two uses without the full form.
  - partial (1 mark): Only the full form, or only one use.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: ATM means Automated Teller Machine. We use it to take out money at any time and to check how much money is in our bank account.
- Marking guide: Accept "Automatic Teller Machine" for the full form. "Any Time Money" is a popular nickname, not the full form: 0 for that part.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.8 l.6-8
- Teacher note: The textbook gives one use (taking out money any time); a second use comes from general knowledge, so any real ATM use is accepted.

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 5. — 3 marks

> What are sacred groves?

- **Answer: Sacred groves are small patches of forest protected by local communities. The trees and wildlife in them are preserved. They are important places for the community to gather, worship and celebrate the beauty of nature.**
- Answer points:
  - Small patches of forest (1 mark)
  - Protected by local communities; trees and wildlife are preserved (1 mark)
  - Places where the community gathers, worships and celebrates nature (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All three points.
  - partial-high (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - partial (1 mark): One point.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Sacred groves are small patches of forest that are protected by the local community. Their trees and animals are not harmed. People gather there to worship and celebrate nature.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.9 l.23-31
- Teacher note: Printed "5.What" with no space, kept.

- **Answer: Dragonfly**
- Also accept: dragonfly · dragonflies · dragon fly · dragon-fly · darning needle · insect · an insect · bhambhiri · bhanbhiri · tuneega · thumbi · thumbee · chuchundri · helicopter insect · damselfly
- Marking guide: Picture 5 shows an insect from above with two pairs of long, clear, veined wings, big round eyes and a long thin body. Dragonfly gets the mark; "insect" is accepted because the question only asks to name the picture. Damselfly (a close relative) is also accepted.
- Source: Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook)

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q12 · 1. — 2 marks

> What is super food? Write the names of any two super food.

- **Answer: Super foods are foods that are very rich in nutrients and keep us healthy and strong, such as millets. Examples: jowar, bajra, ragi, jau (barley).**
- Answer points:
  - Meaning: food rich in nutrients that keeps us healthy (e.g. millets) (1 mark)
  - First correct example (0.5 marks)
  - Second correct example (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Correct meaning and two correct examples.
  - partial-high (1.5 marks): Meaning and one correct example.
  - partial-low (0.5 marks): One correct example only.
  - partial (1 mark): Meaning only, or two examples without the meaning.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Super foods are foods that are full of nutrients and keep us healthy. Millets like jowar and bajra are super foods.
- Marking guide: Examples: jowar, bajra, ragi / nachni / finger millet, jau / barley, millets, kodo, kutki, foxtail millet, amla, moringa / drumstick leaves, spinach, nuts, almonds, walnuts, flax seeds, curd, dates, sprouts. Junk food gets 0.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.6 l.34-41
- Teacher note: Printed "Answers" in the instruction and "any two super food" (singular) kept. The textbook shows millets at "a stall of super food" but does not define the term, so the parent judges the meaning.

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q12 · 2. — 2 marks

> What things should be kept in a first-aid box?

- **Answer: Medicines, mosquito repellent cream, bandages, cotton, antiseptic cream or liquid, band-aids, scissors, a thermometer and medical tape.**
- Answer points:
  - Any two correct items (½ each) (1 mark)
  - Two more correct items (½ each) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Four or more correct first-aid items.
  - partial (1 mark): Two or three correct items (or ½ per item up to 2 marks).
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: A first-aid box should have medicines, bandages, cotton, antiseptic cream and scissors.
- Marking guide: ½ mark per correct item, up to 2 marks. Textbook: medicines, mosquito repellent cream. Also accept: bandage, cotton, gauze, band-aid / plaster, antiseptic cream / liquid (Dettol, Savlon), burn cream, scissors, thermometer, medical tape, ORS, pain-relief spray, tweezers, gloves, ice pack, neem-oil mixture.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.6-9
- Teacher note: The textbook names only medicines and mosquito repellent cream; the other items come from general knowledge, so the parent judges the list.

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 1. — 2 marks

> Different plants and animals are dependent on each other.

- **Answer: Plants give animals food, shelter and oxygen; animals help plants by spreading seeds, carrying pollen and giving manure. Animals also depend on other animals for food (a tiger eats a deer). Everything in nature is connected like a web, so if one part disappears the others suffer.**
- Answer points:
  - How animals depend on plants (food, shelter, oxygen) (1 mark)
  - How plants depend on animals, or how animals depend on each other / the web of life (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Two correct reasons with examples (both directions, or the web of life).
  - partial (1 mark): One correct reason.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Animals depend on plants for food and shelter, like a deer eating grass and birds living in trees. Plants depend on animals to spread their seeds and pollen. A tiger depends on the deer for food, so all living things are connected.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.22 l.7-16; Ch 3 (deev103), p.23 l.3-4

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 2. — 2 marks

> We should avoid eating junk food.

- **Answer: Junk food has high amounts of oil, salt and sugar, so it is not healthy if eaten regularly or in large amounts. It can make us fall ill (obesity, tooth decay, stomach problems) and does not give the body the nutrients it needs.**
- Answer points:
  - Junk food has too much oil, salt and sugar (1 mark)
  - It is not healthy / harms the body (illness, weight gain, tooth decay) / has few nutrients (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says junk food has too much oil, salt or sugar AND that it harms health.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one of the two points.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Junk food like chips and burgers has a lot of oil, salt and sugar. Eating it often makes us unhealthy and can cause illness, so we should avoid it.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.10 l.2-9
- Teacher note: Printed "2.We" (no space), kept.

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 3. — 2 marks

> Drinking sufficient water should be a part of our healthy habits.

- **Answer: Water helps in digesting food and keeps our skin and body healthy. It removes waste from our body through urine, sweat and faeces.**
- Answer points:
  - Water helps digest food / keeps skin and body healthy (1 mark)
  - Water removes waste from the body (urine, sweat, faeces) / keeps the body cool and stops dehydration (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Two correct reasons why water is needed.
  - partial (1 mark): One correct reason.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Water helps us digest food and keeps our skin and body healthy. It also removes waste from our body through urine and sweat.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.12 l.7-17
- Teacher note: Printed "3.Drinking" (no space), kept.

### ⚑ Section 3 · Q14 · Q14 — 5 marks

> Draw 1 junk food , 1 healthy food , a bird and colour it--

- **Answer: Three recognisable drawings — one junk food (e.g. burger, pizza, chips), one healthy food (e.g. apple, banana, carrot, idli) and a bird (e.g. parrot, sparrow, peacock) — all coloured.**
- Answer points:
  - One junk food drawn recognisably (burger, pizza, chips, soft drink, noodles …) (1 mark)
  - One healthy food drawn recognisably (fruit, vegetable, idli, roti, milk …) (1 mark)
  - A bird drawn recognisably (beak, wings, two legs) (1 mark)
  - Drawings neatly coloured (all three) (2 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (5 marks): All three drawings correct and recognisable, and all neatly coloured.
  - partial-high (4 marks): Three correct drawings with rough or incomplete colouring, or two correct drawings well coloured.
  - partial-low (1 mark): Only one correct drawing.
  - partial (2.5 marks): Two correct drawings with some colouring, or three correct drawings with no colouring.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing drawn, or no correct drawing.
- Model answer: A brown-and-yellow burger, a red apple with a green leaf, and a green parrot with a red beak sitting on a branch, all coloured in.
- Marking guide: Printed marks "3+ 2 = 5M": 1 mark for each of the three drawings (3) and 2 marks for colouring. Colouring: 2 if all three drawings are coloured neatly, 1 if only some are coloured or the colouring is very rough, 0 if not coloured. A junk food drawn in the healthy-food place (or the other way round) gets 0 for that drawing. Labels are helpful but not required.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.10 l.5-7; Ch 3 (deev103), p.12 l.1-6
- Teacher note: Printed with spaces before the commas and "--" after "colour it", kept. The paper leaves a blank space for the drawings.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 1) — 2 marks

> Where do we keep our money safe? If we want immediate cash where do we go and withdraw money?

- **Answer: We keep our money safe in a bank. For immediate cash we go to an ATM (or the bank) and withdraw money.**
- Answer points:
  - Money is kept safe in a bank (1 mark)
  - Immediate cash: go to an ATM (the bank counter is also accepted) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Bank for keeping money safe AND ATM (or bank) for immediate cash.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part correct.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part correct.
- Model answer: We keep our money safe in a bank. For immediate cash we go to an ATM and withdraw money.
- Marking guide: Part 1: bank / the bank / in the bank (also "bank account", "savings account"). Part 2: ATM / ATM machine / Automated Teller Machine; "bank" is also accepted, since money can be withdrawn at the bank counter. Accept the Hindi "bank" spelt any way.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.8 l.4-15
- Teacher note: The header prints "Total No. of printed pages: 09", but the paper has 8 pages ("Page 1 of 8" … "Page 8 of 8") and nothing is missing: Q1–Q15 run without a gap and the marks add up to 80. For part 2, both "ATM" and "bank" are defensible, so both get the mark.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 2) — 2 marks

> Identify this bird and write its name. How does this bird move in water?

- **Answer: It is a duck. It swims (paddles) in water with its webbed feet.**
- Answer points:
  - Name: duck (mallard) (1 mark)
  - Moves in water by swimming / paddling with its webbed feet (floating also accepted) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Names the duck AND says it swims / paddles with webbed feet.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part correct (e.g. "duck" but no movement, or "it swims" with a wrong name).
  - none (0 marks): Neither part correct.
- Model answer: This is a duck. It swims in water by paddling with its webbed feet.
- Marking guide: Name: duck, ducks, mallard, mallard duck, wild duck, drake, batakh / bathak / badak (Hindi), bathu (Telugu), vaathu (Tamil), baatu (Kannada), tharavu (Malayalam). Not "swan", "goose" or "hen". Movement: swims, paddles, floats and swims, "uses its webbed feet like oars", "with the help of webbed feet". "Floats" alone gets the mark too.
- Source: Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook); webbed feet: Ch 3 (deev103), p.16 l.17-19
- Teacher note: Ducks are not named in the Chapter 1–5 text; the textbook explains webbed feet for swimming with turtles (Ch 3). This is general knowledge, so the parent checks the wording.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1 · 3) — 2 marks

> What kind of food group is this? Name any two food items from this group.

- **Answer: Body-building foods (protein-rich foods). Any two of: egg, chicken/meat, fish, milk, paneer/cheese, beans/rajma/pulses (dal), peanuts.**
- Answer points:
  - Food group: body-building foods / protein-rich foods (1 mark)
  - First correct food item from this group (0.5 marks)
  - Second correct food item from this group (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Correct food group (body-building / protein) AND two correct food items.
  - partial-high (1.5 marks): Food group correct and only one correct food item.
  - partial-low (0.5 marks): Only one correct food item and nothing else.
  - partial (1 mark): Food group correct but no correct items, or two correct items but the group missing or wrong.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: These are body-building foods (protein foods). Examples: eggs and fish.
- Marking guide: Group: body-building food(s), body building food, protein food(s), protein-rich food, proteins, "food that helps us grow". Items: egg(s), chicken, meat, mutton, fish, milk, cheese, paneer, beans, rajma, kidney beans, pulses, dal, lentils, chana / chickpeas, soybean, tofu, peanuts, groundnuts, almonds, walnuts, curd. "Energy-giving" or "protective" for the group gets 0 for that part.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.7-18
- Teacher note: The textbook calls this group "body-building foods"; "protein" is the word on the printed picture (a shaker labelled PROTEIN, not redrawn here). Accept either name.

  - full (2 marks): Electrician AND one correct tool.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part correct.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part correct.

Tool: screwdriver, pliers / plier / plas, tester / line tester / screwdriver tester, wire cutter, wire stripper, insulation tape / black tape, multimeter, drill, spanner, hammer, ladder, torch. Safety gear he is shown wearing (helmet, rubber gloves) is also accepted, since the question asks what he uses.

- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Solar cooker AND one correct benefit.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part correct.
  - none (0 marks): Neither part correct.
- Model answer: It is a solar cooker. It cooks food with sunlight and does not make smoke, so it does not pollute the environment.
- Marking guide: Name: solar cooker, solar oven, sun cooker, box solar cooker. Benefit: cooks with sunlight; saves gas / LPG / fuel / wood / electricity / money; no smoke or ash; does not pollute; environment-friendly; sunlight is free and never runs out.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q4 · Q4 — 3 marks

> Match the method of cooking and with its name.

- Pairs:
  - Picture 1 → boiling
  - Picture 2 → steaming
  - Picture 3 → grilling
  - Picture 4 → frying
  - Picture 5 → roasting
  - Picture 6 → baking
- **Answer: 1 – boiling; 2 – steaming; 3 – grilling (or roasting); 4 – frying; 5 – roasting (or grilling); 6 – baking.**
- Answer points:
  - Picture 1 (eggs in bubbling water) – boiling (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 2 (food on trays above water, covered) – steaming (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 3 (food on a rack under a hot element) – grilling or roasting (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 4 (patties in oil in a pan) – frying (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 5 (food on a grate over hot coals) – roasting or grilling (0.5 marks)
  - Picture 6 (muffins in an oven) – baking (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All six pictures matched correctly (pictures 3 and 5 may take grilling and roasting either way round).
  - partial (1.5 marks): Three pictures matched correctly (½ each); give ½ for every correct pair.
  - none (0 marks): No correct pair.
- Marking guide: ½ mark per correct pair. Pictures 3 (oven rack under a hot element) and 5 (barbecue grate over coals) can each be called grilling or roasting: accept 3 – grilling, 5 – roasting, or 3 – roasting, 5 – grilling.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.13 l.18-26
- Teacher note: Printed marks are "3 x 1 = 3M", but there are six pictures and six names, so each pair is marked ½ (6 × ½ = 3). The printed instruction has a stray "and" ("cooking and with its name"), kept. Pictures 3 and 5 both show food cooked by direct dry heat on a rack/grate, so grilling and roasting are accepted for either.

- Marking guide: The language panel on the back shows the value in 15 languages; Hindi and English are printed on both sides, making 17 in all. Accept 17, and also 15 (a child who counted only the panel) and 2 (a child who counted only the front: Hindi and English).
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.10 l.42
- Teacher note: The answer depends on what the child counts: 17 on the whole note, 15 in the back panel alone, or 2 on the front alone. All three are accepted.

#### Section 1 · Q5 · c) — 1 mark

> Which bank issues this note?

- **Answer: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**
- Also accept: Reserve Bank of India · Reserve Bank · RBI · R.B.I. · the Reserve Bank of India · Bharatiya Reserve Bank · Bhartiya Rizarv Bank
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.10 l.38-40

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q5 · d) — 1 mark

> Which famous Indian prominent leader’s image is printed on the note?

- **Answer: Mahatma Gandhi**
- Also accept: Mahatma Gandhi · Gandhi · Gandhiji · Gandhi ji · Gandhi Ji · Mahatma Gandhiji · Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi · M.K. Gandhi · MK Gandhi · Bapu · Bapuji · Father of the Nation · Gandhi Bapu
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.10 l.44

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q5 · e) — 1 mark

> Encircle the national emblem of our country on the above note.

- **Answer: The Lion Capital of Ashoka (three lions on a base with a wheel, "Satyamev Jayate" below) on the right side of the front of the note is circled.**

  - full (1 mark): The national emblem (lions on the base with the wheel) on the front of the note is circled.
  - partial (0.5 marks): The circle is near the emblem but also takes in other large parts of the note.
  - none (0 marks): Something else is circled, or nothing is circled.

- Marking guide: Paper-based: the child circles the emblem on the printout. It is on the right side of the FRONT of the note: the lions on a round base with a wheel (Ashoka Chakra), with "सत्यमेव जयते" written under it. 1 mark if the circle is around the emblem (it may include its box); 0 if it circles the portrait, the fort, the value or the spectacles logo.
- Source: Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook)
- Teacher note: The national emblem (Lion Capital of Ashoka) is not in the Chapter 1–5 text; this is general knowledge. Do this on the printed sheet.

### Section 2 — IDENTIFICATION AND CLASSIFICATION (30MARKS) (30 marks)

**Q6 — Who am I? 2 x 1 = 2M**

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q6 · a) — 1 mark

> I am an insect, green in colour. I have three pairs of legs, one pair of antennae to sense surroundings, also sometimes have two pairs of wings. Ans: \_\_\_\_\_\_

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q6 · b) — 1 mark

**Q8 — Circle the one which does not belong to the group. 4 x 1 = 4M**

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q8 · 1. — 1 mark

> Ant Wasp Butterfly Termite

- Options: Ant · Wasp · Butterfly · Termite
- **Answer: Butterfly · Termite**
- Marking guide: Butterfly: ants, wasps and termites live together in colonies (nests) and can bite or sting; a butterfly does not. Termite: ants, wasps and butterflies all visit flowers or feed on sweet things like nectar, while termites eat wood (and termites are the only one not named in the textbook). Either gets the mark.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.17 l.9-11; termite: Class 4 EVS content standard (not in textbook)
- Teacher note: Two answers are defensible: Butterfly (the only one that does not live in a colony) and Termite (the only wood-eater, and not in the textbook). Both are accepted.

#### Section 2 · Q8 · 2. — 1 mark

> Rice Wheat Lemon Maize

- Options: Rice · Wheat · Lemon · Maize
- **Answer: Lemon**
- Marking guide: Rice, wheat and maize are cereals (energy-giving foods); lemon is a fruit (protective food).
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.1-3; Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.19-26

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q8 · 3. — 1 mark

> Marigold Tulsi Amla Ajwain

- Options: Marigold · Tulsi · Amla · Ajwain
- **Answer: Marigold · Amla**
- Marking guide: Marigold: a flower used for colour (natural dye), while tulsi, amla and ajwain are used as medicine / food. Amla: a fruit, while tulsi and ajwain are kept in the textbook's home-remedy table and marigold is a flower. Either gets the mark.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.4 l.20-22; Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.16-19; Ch 5 (deev105), p.9 l.29
- Teacher note: Two answers are defensible: Marigold (a flower used for dye; the others are medicinal plants) and Amla (a fruit, the protective food in Ch 5; tulsi and ajwain are the home-remedy plants in Ch 4). Both are accepted.

**Q9 — Answer the following questions. 5×3=15M**

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 1. — 3 marks

> What is Van Mahotsav? When is it celebrated?

- **Answer: Van Mahotsav is the Tree Planting Festival of India. People plant trees to protect the environment and make the earth greener. It is celebrated every year in the rainy season, from 1 July to 7 July.**
- Answer points:
  - It is the tree planting festival (people plant trees) (1 mark)
  - Why: to protect the environment / make the earth greener (1 mark)
  - When: every year in the rainy season, 1 to 7 July (first week of July) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Says it is the tree planting festival, why trees are planted, and that it is celebrated from 1 to 7 July (rainy season).
  - partial-high (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - partial (1 mark): One of the three points.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Van Mahotsav is the Tree Planting Festival. People plant trees to protect the environment and make the earth greener. It is celebrated every year in the rainy season, from 1st to 7th July.
- Marking guide: For "when", accept "1–7 July", "first week of July", "in July" or "in the rainy season".
- Source: Ch 1 (deev101), p.6 l.2-12

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 2. — 3 marks

> Who is a nature scientist? Write about its role.

- **Answer: A nature scientist is a person who studies plants and animals. Role: observes and studies plants, animals and birds in forests; guides people (like students on a nature trail) in exploring nature; tells us not to harm plants and animals and helps protect them.**
- Answer points:
  - A person who studies plants and animals (nature) (1 mark)
  - Role: observes / studies / identifies plants, animals and birds in their habitat (1 mark)
  - Role: guides others in exploring nature and teaches them to protect it (do not harm plants and animals) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Correct meaning plus two roles.
  - partial-high (2 marks): Correct meaning plus one role, or two roles without the meaning.
  - partial (1 mark): Only the meaning, or only one role.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: A nature scientist is a person who studies plants and animals. Abha Didi, a nature scientist, guided the students through the forest at Pachmarhi, told them about the birds and animals there, and taught them not to harm plants and animals.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.4 l.5-14
- Teacher note: Printed "its role" (for a person) kept. The textbook defines a nature scientist; the roles are drawn from what Abha Didi does in Ch 3, so the parent judges the wording.

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 3. — 3 marks

> What is a balanced diet?

- **Answer: A balanced diet (balanced plate) has food in the right quantities from all three food groups — protective foods (fruits and vegetables) the most, then body-building foods and some energy-giving foods — along with water. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.**
- Answer points:
  - Food from all three food groups (energy-giving, body-building, protective) (1 mark)
  - In the right quantities (more fruits and vegetables, some body-building and energy foods), with water (1 mark)
  - It keeps us healthy, active and strong / helps the body grow (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All three food groups, right quantities, and why it is needed.
  - partial-high (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - partial (1 mark): One point.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: A balanced diet has all three food groups — energy-giving, body-building and protective foods — in the right amounts, with plenty of fruits and vegetables and enough water. It keeps us healthy, active and happy.
- Marking guide: Naming the three groups with an example each also earns the first point.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.8 l.25-30; Ch 5 (deev105), p.8 l.1-5

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 4. — 3 marks

> Write the full form of ATM. Write any two uses of ATM.

- **Answer: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine. Uses: to take out (withdraw) money at any time; to check the bank balance; to deposit money; to get a mini statement; to change the PIN.**
- Answer points:
  - Full form: Automated Teller Machine (1 mark)
  - First use, e.g. take out money any time (1 mark)
  - Second use, e.g. check balance / deposit money / mini statement / change PIN / transfer money (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): Correct full form and two correct uses.
  - partial-high (2 marks): Full form and one use, or two uses without the full form.
  - partial (1 mark): Only the full form, or only one use.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: ATM means Automated Teller Machine. We use it to take out money at any time and to check how much money is in our bank account.
- Marking guide: Accept "Automatic Teller Machine" for the full form. "Any Time Money" is a popular nickname, not the full form: 0 for that part.
- Source: Ch 2 (deev102), p.8 l.6-8
- Teacher note: The textbook gives one use (taking out money any time); a second use comes from general knowledge, so any real ATM use is accepted.

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q9 · 5. — 3 marks

> What are sacred groves?

- **Answer: Sacred groves are small patches of forest protected by local communities. The trees and wildlife in them are preserved. They are important places for the community to gather, worship and celebrate the beauty of nature.**
- Answer points:
  - Small patches of forest (1 mark)
  - Protected by local communities; trees and wildlife are preserved (1 mark)
  - Places where the community gathers, worships and celebrates nature (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (3 marks): All three points.
  - partial-high (2 marks): Two of the three points.
  - partial (1 mark): One point.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Sacred groves are small patches of forest that are protected by the local community. Their trees and animals are not harmed. People gather there to worship and celebrate nature.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.9 l.23-31
- Teacher note: Printed "5.What" with no space, kept.

**Q12 — Answers the following questions. 2 x 2 = 4 M**

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q12 · 1. — 2 marks

> What is super food? Write the names of any two super food.

- **Answer: Super foods are foods that are very rich in nutrients and keep us healthy and strong, such as millets. Examples: jowar, bajra, ragi, jau (barley).**
- Answer points:
  - Meaning: food rich in nutrients that keeps us healthy (e.g. millets) (1 mark)
  - First correct example (0.5 marks)
  - Second correct example (0.5 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Correct meaning and two correct examples.
  - partial-high (1.5 marks): Meaning and one correct example.
  - partial-low (0.5 marks): One correct example only.
  - partial (1 mark): Meaning only, or two examples without the meaning.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Super foods are foods that are full of nutrients and keep us healthy. Millets like jowar and bajra are super foods.
- Marking guide: Examples: jowar, bajra, ragi / nachni / finger millet, jau / barley, millets, kodo, kutki, foxtail millet, amla, moringa / drumstick leaves, spinach, nuts, almonds, walnuts, flax seeds, curd, dates, sprouts. Junk food gets 0.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.6 l.34-41
- Teacher note: Printed "Answers" in the instruction and "any two super food" (singular) kept. The textbook shows millets at "a stall of super food" but does not define the term, so the parent judges the meaning.

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q12 · 2. — 2 marks

> What things should be kept in a first-aid box?

- **Answer: Medicines, mosquito repellent cream, bandages, cotton, antiseptic cream or liquid, band-aids, scissors, a thermometer and medical tape.**
- Answer points:
  - Any two correct items (½ each) (1 mark)
  - Two more correct items (½ each) (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Four or more correct first-aid items.
  - partial (1 mark): Two or three correct items (or ½ per item up to 2 marks).
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: A first-aid box should have medicines, bandages, cotton, antiseptic cream and scissors.
- Marking guide: ½ mark per correct item, up to 2 marks. Textbook: medicines, mosquito repellent cream. Also accept: bandage, cotton, gauze, band-aid / plaster, antiseptic cream / liquid (Dettol, Savlon), burn cream, scissors, thermometer, medical tape, ORS, pain-relief spray, tweezers, gloves, ice pack, neem-oil mixture.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.7 l.6-9
- Teacher note: The textbook names only medicines and mosquito repellent cream; the other items come from general knowledge, so the parent judges the list.

**Q13 — Give reason. 3 x 2 = 6 M**

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 1. — 2 marks

> Different plants and animals are dependent on each other.

- **Answer: Plants give animals food, shelter and oxygen; animals help plants by spreading seeds, carrying pollen and giving manure. Animals also depend on other animals for food (a tiger eats a deer). Everything in nature is connected like a web, so if one part disappears the others suffer.**
- Answer points:
  - How animals depend on plants (food, shelter, oxygen) (1 mark)
  - How plants depend on animals, or how animals depend on each other / the web of life (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Two correct reasons with examples (both directions, or the web of life).
  - partial (1 mark): One correct reason.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Animals depend on plants for food and shelter, like a deer eating grass and birds living in trees. Plants depend on animals to spread their seeds and pollen. A tiger depends on the deer for food, so all living things are connected.
- Source: Ch 3 (deev103), p.22 l.7-16; Ch 3 (deev103), p.23 l.3-4

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 2. — 2 marks

> We should avoid eating junk food.

- **Answer: Junk food has high amounts of oil, salt and sugar, so it is not healthy if eaten regularly or in large amounts. It can make us fall ill (obesity, tooth decay, stomach problems) and does not give the body the nutrients it needs.**
- Answer points:
  - Junk food has too much oil, salt and sugar (1 mark)
  - It is not healthy / harms the body (illness, weight gain, tooth decay) / has few nutrients (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says junk food has too much oil, salt or sugar AND that it harms health.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one of the two points.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Junk food like chips and burgers has a lot of oil, salt and sugar. Eating it often makes us unhealthy and can cause illness, so we should avoid it.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.10 l.2-9
- Teacher note: Printed "2.We" (no space), kept.

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q13 · 3. — 2 marks

> Drinking sufficient water should be a part of our healthy habits.

- **Answer: Water helps in digesting food and keeps our skin and body healthy. It removes waste from our body through urine, sweat and faeces.**
- Answer points:
  - Water helps digest food / keeps skin and body healthy (1 mark)
  - Water removes waste from the body (urine, sweat, faeces) / keeps the body cool and stops dehydration (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Two correct reasons why water is needed.
  - partial (1 mark): One correct reason.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing correct.
- Model answer: Water helps us digest food and keeps our skin and body healthy. It also removes waste from our body through urine and sweat.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.12 l.7-17
- Teacher note: Printed "3.Drinking" (no space), kept.

**Q14 — Draw 1 junk food , 1 healthy food , a bird and colour it-- 3+ 2 = 5M**

#### ⚑ Section 3 · Q14 · Q14 — 5 marks

> Draw 1 junk food , 1 healthy food , a bird and colour it--

- **Answer: Three recognisable drawings — one junk food (e.g. burger, pizza, chips), one healthy food (e.g. apple, banana, carrot, idli) and a bird (e.g. parrot, sparrow, peacock) — all coloured.**
- Answer points:
  - One junk food drawn recognisably (burger, pizza, chips, soft drink, noodles …) (1 mark)
  - One healthy food drawn recognisably (fruit, vegetable, idli, roti, milk …) (1 mark)
  - A bird drawn recognisably (beak, wings, two legs) (1 mark)
  - Drawings neatly coloured (all three) (2 marks)
- Rubric:
  - full (5 marks): All three drawings correct and recognisable, and all neatly coloured.
  - partial-high (4 marks): Three correct drawings with rough or incomplete colouring, or two correct drawings well coloured.
  - partial-low (1 mark): Only one correct drawing.
  - partial (2.5 marks): Two correct drawings with some colouring, or three correct drawings with no colouring.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing drawn, or no correct drawing.
- Model answer: A brown-and-yellow burger, a red apple with a green leaf, and a green parrot with a red beak sitting on a branch, all coloured in.
- Marking guide: Printed marks "3+ 2 = 5M": 1 mark for each of the three drawings (3) and 2 marks for colouring. Colouring: 2 if all three drawings are coloured neatly, 1 if only some are coloured or the colouring is very rough, 0 if not coloured. A junk food drawn in the healthy-food place (or the other way round) gets 0 for that drawing. Labels are helpful but not required.
- Source: Ch 5 (deev105), p.10 l.5-7; Ch 3 (deev103), p.12 l.1-6
- Teacher note: Printed with spaces before the commas and "--" after "colour it", kept. The paper leaves a blank space for the drawings.

> Madhya Pradesh
